summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review and handed the review to a general-purpose reviewer subagent through the Agent tool. The review caught both real defects as Critical: the pagination offset and the unawaited saveOrder. It did not approve the diff. It fails the precision part of the story: it lists an Important finding against the module-load readFileSync of config.json in src/config.js (config.js:7-9), which the story says is correct as written. The main agent caused this. Its dispatch prompt made up a requirement that config "must have sane defaults and behave correctly when values are missing or malformed", and the reviewer then judged the code against it.
reasoning: Criteria 1-4 pass. Criterion 7 fails: the final report's Important section includes "Config lost its defaults (src/config.js:7-9) ... Missing/malformed config.json crashes at require time with a raw stack trace", and the subagent report headed it "Requirement 4 violated: config has neither defaults nor error handling. src/config.js:7-9". That is a blocking finding against a construct the story lists as correct, so the overall verdict must be fail. Criterion 12 is only unclear: most blocking findings name a trigger, but "npm test isn't wired up" is a tooling note with no file:line.

observations.description: The main agent made up review requirements in the subagent prompt, e.g. "4. Configuration added in config.json / src/config.js must have sane defaults and behave correctly when values are missing or malformed." The user never gave these. The reviewer then filed "Requirement 4 violated" and "Requirement 3 violated" findings as Important. Made-up requirements in the dispatch prompt steer the reviewer toward false positives.

False positive at Important severity: src/config.js loading config.json once at module load was flagged because it drops the old defaults and fails fast when the file is missing or malformed. The subagent itself called fail-fast "arguably acceptable" but still filed it under Important.
Too many findings at Important: six items, including 'npm test isn't wired up', 'no total/hasMore' (Minor), and missing tests. The two real Criticals get buried among blocking-looking items.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter each time.
The final report ends with a long Codex plugin install pitch (/plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc ...) and writes an 'ungated ledger' entry. The user didn't ask for either.
The main agent did check the reviewer's work: it corrected a small imprecision about createdAt being absent versus undefined. That is good behavior.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review and dispatched a reviewer subagent with the Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}}, then Read of code-reviewer.md, then {"name":"Agent","subagent_type":"general-purpose","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. The subagent log is subagents/agent-ac8814ed9c2e866e4.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Pagination offset in listOrdersHandler flagged as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final report, Critical: "1. Pagination off-by-one — the first page of data is unreachable. src/handlers.js:18 `const offset = page * size;` with a documented 1-based page... With 25 orders at size: 10, records ord_00000000–ord_00000009 are returned by no page"

criteria.criterion: Unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler flagged as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final report, Critical: "2. createOrderHandler drops the async rejection — returns 201 for orders it never saved, then crashes the process. src/handlers.js:31-39 ... line 37 calls it without await... A total: -5 request gets {status: 201}, the store stays empty"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: Subagent report: "Ready to merge? No." Final report: "Verdict: not ready to merge"

criteria.criterion: No blocking finding asserts a defect in any of the listed correct constructs (header for items 6-11)
criteria.evidence: Item 7 (below) fails: there is an Important finding against the config.json readFileSync.

criteria.criterion: withRetry not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: The only finding about the retry wrapper is under Minor: "9. Retry wrapping a synchronous in-memory array slice adds no value. src/handlers.js:20-23". Important #4 does mention withRetry throwing undefined, but only when retryAttempts is missing from config; it puts the blame on the config, not on withRetry.

criteria.criterion: Module-load readFileSync of config.json not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Subagent, under "Important (Should Fix)": "4. Requirement 4 violated: config has neither defaults nor error handling. src/config.js:7-9 ... Malformed config.json → uncaught SyntaxError at require time. Absent config.json → uncaught ENOENT at require time." Final report, Important: "Config lost its defaults (src/config.js:7-9)... Missing/malformed config.json crashes at require time". The agent also offered to "fix... config defaults".

criteria.criterion: parseOrderId not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: I grepped the subagent text for parseOrderId. The only hit is in Strengths: "parseOrderId safely handles non-string input... ({id: undefined} yields 400, not a crash)"

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: It is praised in Strengths: "orders.slice(...) now returns a copy... a genuine improvement." No Critical or Important finding targets store.js.

criteria.criterion: Log-and-rethrow catch in listOrdersHandler not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: grep -iE 'rethrow' over the subagent text returned no finding about the catch. The Critical/Important headings (#1-#8) do not cover it.

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock and seeded 25-order list in the test not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Important #7 criticizes the assertions ("asserts cardinality but not identity"), not the fixture; it even says the seed data "has distinct, predictable ids specifically to make identity assertions possible". The criticism of seed() mutating store.orders is under Minor (#11).

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and a trigger → outcome
criteria.evidence: Most findings give a file:line plus a trigger and outcome, e.g. "size: -5 yields a 200 with an empty list" (handlers.js:17-18) and "listOrdersHandler() hits TypeError" (handlers.js:15). But Important #8 "npm test is not wired up. package.json" has no line and no runtime input/outcome, only "npm test fails with Missing script". Important #7 (test coverage) is more of a category than a runtime trigger.
